2. What the list measures. supervisor.rs placeholder_plan builds "identified" from the org's HEAD name (not_a_name(name)) plus the org's total mention count (per_org). It does not say what each mention is named.

3. What the fold reads. project.rs drop_decision classes each party by the names published in that notice's own party section. It drops a party only when every one of those names is VoidLot, Placeholder or Blank. The org's head name and its bound identifier play no part in that decision.

4. What the 28 mentions are named. Issue 511 item 7 and issue 524 both say the org's 28 remaining mentions read 'Vergabekammer bei der Bezirksregierung'. That name has no form section reference, so section_reference_pointer cannot match it, and no stem or whole value matches it. Unit 6 (eefbd64) adds nothing that would match it either. It classes as name, so those parties are kept.

5. The fold has already kept them twice. The org had 46 mentions in dry 2265/2266 and 28 after unit 3's wet (2270/2271), which dropped the 18 's.o.'-named slots. It stayed at 28 in residual 2273, in u4 and u45 dry, after the units 4+5 wet 2306/2307 (u45/plan-residual.json), and in this u6 dry. Both wets re-queued all of this org's notices and kept the same 28.

6. The org survives too. With 28 kept mentions, sweep-orphan-orgs will not remove org 22713056.

7. Why this is not the stop shape. The runbook stops when a placeholder slot's identifier keys a real supplier. Here the identifier is the chamber's phone number, and the slots that carried 's.o.' were dropped back in unit 3. They point at a body named elsewhere in the same notice. The chamber's real-named mentions stay.

- Accounting for the wet: by_class counts these 28 as placeholder mentions (part of the 1,956), but the fold will keep them. Subtract 28 from the drop-class floor, or the wet's retired count will look 28 short.
